value.prompt: Choose an initial weapon modification for your construct's unarmed attack

backfillRows.why: innovation-2 (Breakthrough Modifications, Advanced Weaponry) prints "Choose one of your construct's unarmed attacks to gain your choice of one initial weapon modification, chosen any initial weapon modifications to which you have access." The record carried only actionCost.passive + otherTags, so the pick could not be stored, applied or shown. The eleven options are exactly the level-1 weapon-innovation-modification classFeatures in core.json. No option carries a grant: applying the chosen modification's weaponTraits to a COMPANION's unarmed attack has no reader (applyWeaponRiders walks inventory WeaponItems only), so the row records the answer and claims nothing more. Reader added in batch 036: buildCharacter now resolvePicks the chosen inventor modifications, and the Builder mounts an EffectChoicesPicker for them.

findings.note: Row + reader. The reader half (build.ts resolvePick over build.inventorModifications, Builder.tsx picker) is code; without it the field would be authored, stored and ignored, which is the defect the finding names.

Row only; no code change. The reader (activeStateGrants -> grantSources -> additive land grant) already exists and is pinned by a test on a built character with the field patched in memory. CLOSER, gate-red round: this finding's row (classFeatures/hyper-boosters.whileActive = [{state:'overdrive',speeds:{land:10}}]) was APPLIED from this spec in the first pass and is what shipped core.json held; the gate-red group red-inventor-modification-rows then had to recalibrate it to land:5 because batch 036's own requiresModification row makes speed-boosters a hard prerequisite, so every hyper-boosters number is a delta over the speed-boosters number underneath it and derive.ts ADDS the two. Both specs then wrote the same key classFeatures/hyper-boosters/whileActive, and precheck (1) in scripts/wg-batch-run.mjs hard-refuses a duplicate key across the manifest ("resolve by hand, the applier will not merge"). Per the "two findings on the same record+field must be merged into ONE row" rule the two are merged into the SURVIVING row, which is the superseding one in work/.b036-rows-red-inventor-modification-rows.json (finding "gap E — speed-boosters Overdrive step"): it carries supersedes:true and the whole superseded value merged in with only its number changed. The row is removed here, not from there. The finding's verdict is unaffected — the close derives MATCHES from the teach line in work/.b036-report-engine.txt, and the delivery for hyper-boosters#overdrive is the merged row.

backfillRows.why: innovation-5 (Hyper Boosters) prints "You must have the speed boosters modification to select this modification." Nothing gated the pick and hyper-boosters' landSpeedBonus is deliberately the +5 DELTA over speed-boosters' own +5, so metallic-reactance + hyper-boosters was a legal build here that walked at +5 feet against a printed +10. requiresModification is a new ClassFeature field read by inventorModificationOptions (batch 036); enforcing the prerequisite is what makes the delta encoding true.

findings.note: Row + new reader. Field and reader are code (types.ts, build.ts, shared.tsx); the row is the one record the finding covers. Five sibling modifications print the same kind of clause and are named as a lane note in the report, NOT authored here.

backfillRows.why: feat-5835 (Animalistic Brutality) prints "Your unarmed attack from bestial rage gains one of the following traits until you stop raging: backswing, forceful, parry, razing, or sweep… You can choose a different trait each time you use Animalistic Brutality." A trait with an off switch is a mode (owner ruling Q11): DefenseGrants.unarmedTraits is read off the owned RECORD and would hand the barbarian all five traits permanently. One mode per printed trait, sharing an exclusiveGroup so only one is on at a time, gated to the feat. ModeDef.unarmedTraits is the new field batch 036 hoisted and applyUnarmedRiders now reads.

findings.note: Five rows + a new reader. `fromRecord: 'animal-instinct'` is the same gate batch 035 used for the instinct's spec-die step, so the trait lands on the bestial-rage attacks and on nothing else the barbarian happens to own. The modes are gated on the FEAT, so contentGatedModes offers them only to a barbarian who took Animalistic Brutality; no `predefined` flag is needed (isGated is what puts an authored mode in the panel's predefined list).

ROW WITHDRAWN BY THE VERIFIER (batch 036, engine). The finding's claim — and the builder's row `feats/armored-resistance.resistances` — rest on a sweep that never looked in the core.json MODES bucket. `modes/armored-resistance` already ships and already delivers exactly this printed sentence: {feats:['armored-resistance'], duration:'while you Intercept an Attack in medium or heavy armor', resistances:[{type:'physical', value:'floor(@actor.level/2)'}]}. It is gated content (contentGatedModes picks it up off the `feats` gate), modeRelevant offers it to a guardian-archetype character who took the feat, and toggling it puts physical resistance 5 on a 10th-level character's headline total. With the builder's row applied ON TOP, deriveDefenses().sources['resistance:physical'] returns TWO lines, both named 'Armored Resistance', both applied — the same sentence answered twice, which is the defect the builder's own CROSS-FILE GAP A objects to for hyper-boosters. The standing rule is REUSE the lane, not rebuild it; the mode is the better carrier because it is a toggle that produces a real number when the reaction is actually used, while an `against` line can only ever be prose beside the number. The instruments family's wg-diff settle for this record explicitly rests on the mode being the carrier ('the printed resistance is delivered by modes/armored-resistance … which is why `defense` is already on our side of the row'), so authoring a second carrier would also undercut their settle's stated premise. Verdict: the finding is DONE by the shipped lane and needs NO row. test/batch036-engine.test.ts now pins the SHIPPED mode instead of a patched-in field.

Code-only. The payload is already authored — items/energy-resistant.effectChoices ships all four energy branches — and the defect was that nothing read it once the rune was ETCHED: resolvedItemPassives resolves only for an inventory ROW that is in use, and etching consumes that row, while the DefenseGrants walk never called propertyRuneDefs at all. derive.ts now folds every etched property rune's defences (RuneDef.passiveEffects plus the rune item's resolved choice) into the walk, and the Living Rune body rune with it. Adding a runes/energy-resistant passiveEffects row would have been the wrong answer: it cannot carry the crafter's four-way choice, and it would have left every other choice-carrying rune still dead.
